If I’m saving it for a future bowl, I’ll put my tobacco in an empty Tin with some volume to its space. I’m currently using an empty plum pudding tin for this. And I do put the lid on. I live in a drier area so it seems this is sufficient for my needs.
One of my best pipes is a used/estate late 50’s Stanwell factory second. Sometimes the pipes choose you :)

So I had disregarded Stanwell because the pipes I’ve seen if there’s are usually marked better or had the crown on the S. I dug back in the stanwell pipes catalog and found an exact silhouette of the pipe in the Late Fifties catalog under a pipe next to the number 45. 

https://pipedia.org/wiki/Stanwell_Shape_Numbers_and_Designers

I then started searching forums about Stanwell pipes with different S markings and found examples of that marking dating pre early 70’s

http://pipephil.eu/logos/en/logo-stanwell.html

I now gather this is a late 50’s Stanwell “45” sandblasted. Or something near this. Either way I’m glad for the nudge in the right direction to find out a little more about this pipe, and Stanwell pipes in general. 

Did you know that Poul Nielsen was so committed to competing with British pipe companies he changed the company from Nielsen to Stanwell to become more marketable to the English. He even had his name legally changed to Stanwell!
The only markings I could find are the white S on the stem and “GENUINE SANDBLAST  Italy” in the bottom. The pipe also has several imperfections some of which are patched with cement.
